## Functional identification

The sequence encodes a **delta-9 fatty-acid desaturase**, specifically matching *Caenorhabditis elegans* FAT-6 (**UniProt G5EGN2**) exactly: 339/339 residues, 100% identity and coverage.

It is a small, highly hydrophobic **multipass membrane enzyme**, consistent with localization in the **endoplasmic-reticulum membrane**. The sequence contains four strongly predicted transmembrane helices and conserved histidine-rich regions characteristic of membrane fatty-acid desaturases.

## Catalytic activity

The enzyme introduces a **cis double bond at the Δ9 position** of saturated fatty acyl-CoA substrates.

The preferred reaction is:

\[
\text{stearoyl-CoA} + O_2 + 2H^+ + 2\,\text{reduced cytochrome }b_5
\rightarrow
\text{oleoyl-CoA} + 2H_2O + 2\,\text{oxidized cytochrome }b_5
\]

In systematic terms:

\[
\text{octadecanoyl-CoA} \rightarrow (9Z)\text{-octadecenoyl-CoA}
\]

The enzyme can also desaturate palmitoyl-CoA:

\[
\text{palmitoyl-CoA} \rightarrow \text{palmitoleoyl-CoA}
\]

## Cofactor and reaction class

- **Enzyme class:** oxidoreductase  
- **EC:** 1.14.19.1 / 1.14.19.-  
- **Metal requirement:** non-heme iron, likely in a diiron catalytic center  
- **Electron donor system:** cytochrome \(b_5\)-dependent  
- **Oxidant:** molecular oxygen  
- **Products:** monounsaturated fatty acyl-CoA plus water  

### Summary

This protein is an **ER membrane-bound, iron-dependent Δ9 fatty-acyl-CoA desaturase**. Its principal function is conversion of **stearoyl-CoA to cis-oleoyl-CoA**, thereby producing monounsaturated fatty acids used in membrane lipids and triacylglycerol biosynthesis.
